newsitem.title: USA: CME Dow Jones Taiwan index trades 581 in first day.
newsitem.headline: CME Dow Jones Taiwan index trades 581 in first day.

text.p: Volume in Dow Jones Taiwan stock index futures .XDT at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange totaled 581 contracts in their first trading session Wednesday night on the GLOBEX after-hours electronic trading system, the CME said Thursday.
"Strong volume from day one proves us right in gauging the demand for this index," CME chairman Jack Sandner said in a statement.

A similar contract which debuted at the same time on the Singapore International Monetary Exchange, based on Morgan Stanley's Taiwan stock index .MSTW, traded an estimated 500 contracts in its first trading session.

A primary market-maker for the Dow Jones Taiwan stock index options in Chicago said the CME contracts' volume in dollar terms also surpassed SIMEX's volume. He said that in dollar terms about $25 million worth of contracts traded through the GLOBEX terminals, while SIMEX traded $15.5 million worth.
"You have two competing indexes, and in dollar terms the Dow Jones index had more volume," said Judson Ellis, a partner in Hull Trading Company.

"You have fund managers who want cheap access to the market," Ellis said. "A lot of volume is stemming from the hedging of equity swap positions. They have positions on equity swaps that they manage better and more cheaply by using futures."
The CME's March Dow Jones Taiwan stock index, the lead contract month, settled its first GLOBEX session unchanged at 173.50 points. Currently, the cash index is at 172.74.
The CME's contracts will trade exclusively on GLOBEX, and will begin trade their normal hours of 1430 to 1030 CST (2030 to 1630 GMT) on Mondays through Thursdays.
The contract will trade from 1730 to 1030 CST (2330 to 1630 GMT) on Sundays, and from 1830 to 2100 CST (0030 to 0300 GMT) on Fridays. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
